title: The Ghost in the Machine has an American accent: value conflict in GPT-3.
findings: The paper found that GPT-3's outputs can mutate the embedded values of input texts to align more closely with dominant US values. In a religious context, when given a French text on secularism, the model generated an output that framed the policy as an 'anti-Muslim manifesto' and against freedom, reflecting a US-centric interpretation rather than the original French one. The paper also cites prior research indicating GPT-3's bias in associating 'Muslims' with violence far more frequently than 'Christians'.

measurement_description: The benchmark measured value mutation and stereotyping bias. Specifically, it assessed GPT-3's stereotyping bias by associating Muslims with violence (citing previous work) and evaluated how the model altered the value of French secularism, particularly in the context of Islam, framing it as an 'anti-Muslim manifesto'.
